title: Approve and Publish Content
readerIntent: Configure and execute an approval-driven Staged-to-Online content publication without introducing parallel publishing behavior.
priorKnowledge: Understand CMS catalogs, versioning, Workflow, nPublish, cache, search, and separate Staged and Online runtimes.
owner: CMS owns content, Workflow owns approval progress, nPublish owns publication lifecycle, and CMS target adapter owns authenticated deployment
summary: A business user edits versioned Staged content, associates the exact change set with a workflow, completes manual and automatic actions, and publishes the approved version through nPublish to a separate non-versioned Online authority.

sections.heading: Example: publish a campaign page
paragraphs: An editor updates a campaign page and its banner components in the Staged CMS. A workflow validates links automatically, asks a content manager for manual approval, and after final approval requests publication of those exact versions to the Online CMS used by the storefront.

sections.heading: 1. Configure the two authorities
items: Staged and Online run as different systems or schemas, even when both are tested locally.
Enable version variants only for publishable modules/schemas in Staged. Versioning is configuration-driven; unrelated schemas such as ordinary user data do not become versioned automatically.
Online does not activate version variants and stores only the deployed target form served to customers.

Configure authenticated target transport, target alias, dependency/validation rules, workflow provider, version provider, domain adapter, cache/search refresh, timeouts, limits, and redacted observability.

sections.heading: 2. Author and submit
items: Create or update the page and components in the correct Staged Site and content catalog.
Persist immutable versions and identify the exact tenant, domain, item codes, versions, dependencies, and target.
Create a workflow carrier referencing that change set. Workflow actions may be manual or automatic according to the configured business process.
Do not copy mutable draft content into workflow state or create a CMS-specific approval engine.

sections.heading: 3. Validate and approve
items: Run owning-domain validation and dependency checks for page, template, slots/components, media/references, locale, Site/catalog context, and target readiness.
Automatic actions may validate or enrich; manual actions may review, reject, request changes, or approve.
Workflow owns the approval decision and history. nPublish consumes the decision but never duplicates workflow state.
A rejection or changed source version returns the change to authoring/revalidation; an earlier approval never authorizes a later mutable draft.

sections.heading: 4. Publish and serve
items: Create the publication request with optimistic revision and the exact approved versions.
nPublish validates state, bounded dependencies, manifest, authorization, and configured providers, then invokes the CMS domain/target adapter.
The adapter deploys through authenticated Online transport; it never writes the Online database directly.
Record the authoritative transition journal and safe audit projection, then invalidate or refresh Online cache and reconcile search through their existing contracts.
The storefront resolves its Site/catalog context and serves only the Online published form.

sections.heading: 5. Failure, reconciliation, and rollback
items: A target timeout can leave completion unknown. Query/reconcile Online state before retrying; idempotent terminal replay prevents duplicate transitions.
Repair missing audit projections from the authoritative publication journal without inventing a second publication source of truth.
Rollback deploys an approved previous version through the same auditable adapter path where supported; it is not a direct database restore.
Reconcile cache, search, export, media/references, and storefront visibility after recovery or rollback. External effects may require explicit business compensation.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Author, version, submit, automatic action, manual approve/reject/change request, exact-version activation, Online visibility, cache invalidation, search reconciliation, and storefront rendering.

Unauthorized/wrong-tenant/wrong-Site, invalid dependency, stale revision, changed source after approval, duplicate request/replay, unavailable workflow/version/domain/target provider, target timeout/outage, partial publication, and unknown completion.

Restart, reconciliation, rollback, compensation, audit redaction, staged/online isolation, performance, concurrent publication, contract, integration, modular topology, upgrade, accessibility of BackOffice guidance, and regression.
Product or another publishable domain reuses nPublish but contributes its own dependency resolver, validation, manifest, and target adapter rather than a parallel state machine.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
paragraphs: Contribute project-specific reviewers, workflow actions, content types, and publication mappings through later WCMS, Workflow, CMS, and nPublish layers while preserving their existing authority boundaries.
items: Do not edit reusable publishing framework source, activate a rejected carrier, or create a second staged-to-online publication path.
Verify manual and automatic actions, approval and rejection, idempotent retry, target validation, authorization, failure recovery, rollback, and regression.
Rollback restores the previous versioned workflow definition and publication mapping through the same governed authority.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How To Approve And Publish Content
paragraphs: This guide explains the implemented Nodics content-publishing flow in plain language. It is for business users who manage content, operators who configure Staged and Online systems, and developers who customize publishing.

sections.heading: What This Capability Does
paragraphs: Nodics keeps editable content away from the public Online system. A content editor works in **Staged**, sends a complete change set for review, and an approved workflow publishes one immutable release to **Online**. A rejected change does not alter Online content. An operator can roll back to the previous deployed release.

The current backend capability is implemented and tested. A BackOffice visual client is not part of this implementation yet; an authorized client can invoke the same module APIs and workflow contracts later without changing their authority.

sections.heading: Responsibilities And Authority
paragraphs:
| Capability | Authority |
| --- | --- |
| Review steps and approval decision | `gContent/wcms` using the existing workflow engine |
| Generic publication states, revisions, journal, and audit projection | `gFramework/nPublish` |
| CMS dependency rules and immutable delivery snapshot | `gContent/cms` |
| Editable content versions | Staged versioned database variants |
| Deployed manifests and active delivery pointer | Online CMS database |
| Human login and permissions | Profile and the normal user authentication flow |
| Staged-to-Online deployment | Internal module authentication, never a human password |
Do not add a second workflow engine, publication state machine, version store, or Online pointer. Project code should extend these owners.

sections.heading: Select Which Schemas Are Versioned
paragraphs: Versioning is opt-in at module/schema level. A Staged catalog or CMS schema can set `isVersionedEnabled: true` through its layered schema configuration while unrelated schemas, such as users, remain non-versioned. The Online deployment uses the ordinary non-versioned schemas and stores only deployed target forms.
Do not copy base schemas merely to add common properties. Nodics merges base schema properties at runtime; override only the setting or business property that differs.

sections.heading: Customize The Workflow
paragraphs: Projects can layer new reviewers, actions, and channels over the existing WCMS workflow data. Keep the final automatic action connected only to the successful approval path. A rejection path must never call publication activation.
Project-specific content types, renderer keys, templates, and sample data belong in the project module. Reusable CMS must not contain one customer's page model or executable frontend paths.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
paragraphs:
| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Publication fails before deployment | Exact source versions, dependency limits, renderer keys, and workflow release input |
| Target connection is unavailable | `servers.<connectionName>`, host/port, internal token readiness, timeout, retry, and circuit diagnostics |
| Online rejects deployment | `runtimeRole: 'ONLINE'`, `publishEnabled: false`, manifest size, integrity, and supported contract version |
| Online returns no page | Active pointer for tenant/site/path/locale/channel/access mode and `cms.publication.enabled` rollout order |
| A rejected change appears Online | Verify the workflow graph: only the approved terminal action may call nPublish |
| Rollback is unavailable | A previous Online manifest must have been deployed and captured by the later publication |

sections.heading: Verify A Change
paragraphs: Run focused contracts first:

```bash
node gFramework/nPublish/test/publicationLifecycleService.test.js
node gFramework/nPublish/test/publicationAtomicAuditContract.test.js
node gFramework/nPublish/test/publicationAuditReconciliationService.test.js
node gContent/cms/test/cmsPublicationManifestContract.test.js
node gContent/wcms/test/wcmsPublicationWorkflowContract.test.js
```
Build the Staged server so generated version-aware services match its active module set, then run the real modular topology proof:

```bash
env SERVER=cmsStagedServer npm run build
npm run test:topology:modular
```

The modular test verifies separate processes and databases, approval, rejection, replay idempotency, a second release, target restart recovery, and rollback. Also run the repository's normal documentation, generated-context, and regression suites before release.
